quotes.text: Teams is not just a collaboration tool. It is a coordination layer. Coordination layers become noisy when the underlying organization is fragmented.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes Teams activity as a measure of coordination pressure rather than collaboration health.

quotes.text: Decision latency is hard to see because it accumulates in the gaps between visible actions like the space between a message and an answer or the time between a decision and the final version.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines decision latency in concrete, everyday terms.

quotes.text: Low quality AI output is often not an AI quality problem first. It is an organizational memory problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shifts the blame for weak Copilot answers from the model to the content and ownership layer.

quotes.text: That's why permission reviews are not just a compliance exercise. They are a structural audit. They tell you where the business still depends on individuals, hidden pathways and unexamined inheritance.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Turns permission reviews from a checkbox into a diagnostic of how the organization really works.

quotes.text: If one person holds the relationship map and the access rights, your performance is not resilient, it is concentrated, and concentration is risk.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the hidden single-point-of-failure risk behind celebrated key people.

chapters.title: The organization leaders think they run
Signal one: Teams shows coordination pressure
Signal two: SharePoint and OneDrive reveal how knowledge moves
Signal three: identity and permission drift define the real org
Case study: the well-structured, slow organization
Decision latency, rework, shadow systems and why Copilot becomes a mirror
Four steps: map decisions, trace data, find hidden owners, simplify

takeaways: High Teams activity, duplicated files in SharePoint and OneDrive, and drifting permissions are signals of structural compensation, not proof of collaboration maturity.
Copilot reasons over the content and access your environment actually contains, so fragmented knowledge and permission drift turn it into a mirror of organizational problems rather than a fix.
Start by mapping one real decision end to end, tracing its files and versions, identifying hidden owners and measuring friction, then simplify the environment before scaling it.
hook: Your org chart, governance model and adoption dashboards may describe an organization that no longer exists. This episode is for IT leaders, Microsoft 365 architects and change practitioners who see high usage but slow, heavy work. Learn how to read Teams, SharePoint and permission signals to find the real organization and fix it before Copilot amplifies the gaps.
